Hi Olivia (and Jake) 

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view and next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points you shared
- Strict PII/PHI handling: must ensure names, DOBs, SSNs, medical identifiers are never stored in cleartext and are redacted or tokenized.
- Retention policy: default retention needs to be ~90 days for searchable logs, with the ability to purge earlier on request.
- Auditability: exports of immutable audit logs for any request/response sequence, including who accessed what and when (for audits).
- Redaction requirements: need deterministic redaction (consistent mapping for de-identification) plus proof of redaction for compliance.
- Deployment preference: strong interest in Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.

Current stack you described
- Front-end: patient portal (React) + API gateway
- Backend: internal microservices on AWS (EKS) and an internal data store (Postgres)
- Logging/observability: Splunk for logs, Okta for SSO

Success criteria for a pilot
1) Demonstrate end-to-end encryption and KMS integration for keys (bring-your-own-key).
2) Show audit log exports for a 30-day window in a format your security team accepts.
3) Redaction pipeline that removes PHI from stored outputs while allowing analytics on metadata.
4) Pilot latency within 200ms p95 for typical request sizes and cost estimates for 100k requests/month.

Proposed next steps
- I attached a short SOC2 summary and a rough data flow diagram we sketched during the call.
- Rishi will follow up with a technical note on redaction approaches and what we recommend for on-client vs on-server tokenization. (cc: Rishi)
- If you can, please share your security questionnaire and procurement timeline  Jake, you mentioned Q3 procurement.
- Schedule: we can stand up a 2-week pilot environment (Dedicated or Private) once we align on the mutual action plan.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (summary), data_flow_diagram.png (sketch)

Thanks again  Ill set up the MAP doc and link it here by tomorrow.

Olivia  quick technical clarifications and options we discussed on the call:

Redaction/tokenization options- Client-side redaction: best for minimizing PII entering any Redwood runtime. We provide SDK hooks and recommended regex/pattern libraries. This approach leaves you full control but requires changes to your client pipeline.
- Server-side deterministic tokenization: we replace PII with consistent tokens (hash+salt or reversible tokenization behind KMS). This enables linkability for analytics while keeping cleartext out of logs/storage. Tokens are stored encrypted and access-controlled.

Retention & audit logs- Retention policies can be applied by tag (e.g., patient-record, clinical-note) and enforced by our metadata store; configurable per-tenant.
- Audit logs: immutable append-only logs with sequence numbers and signed entries (HMAC). Exports available in NDJSON or CSV. We can stream to your Splunk instance or provide an S3 export with server-side encryption.

KMS & key management- Support for BYOK (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. Keys can be rotated; old blobs remain decryptable while tokens maintain referential integrity.

Proof of redaction- We generate transformation manifests: for each processed request we can store a hashed manifest (SHA256 of canonicalized metadata + timestamp + operation) and sign it with a service key. That manifest is exportable for auditors and can be verified against stored audit logs.

Next steps from engineering
1) Ill drop a short tech note with example manifests and a sample NDJSON audit export schema.
2) Well prepare a secure share for the full SOC2 report and our BA template.
3) If you prefer client-side redaction, we can provide a lightweight SDK sample to test on a dev environment in <72 hours.
